evals.prompt: Generate narration clips for this explainer. Segments are in evals/files/segments.json. Write WAVs into /tmp/officekit-tts-eval-narration using the repo's local Kokoro path. Default voice af_heart, 0.25s padding between clips.
evals.expected_output: Runs uv sync only if needed, then uv run python skills/text-to-speech/scripts/synthesize.py with the given JSON, output dir, voice, and padding. Writes one WAV per id plus manifest.json. Does not create a project-local venv or call a cloud TTS API.
expectations: Invokes skills/text-to-speech/scripts/synthesize.py via uv run from the repository root
Does not create or activate a virtualenv under projects/ or the skill directory
Does not use ElevenLabs, OpenAI, or other cloud TTS
Produces one WAV per segment id plus a measured manifest.json
Passes padding as timing metadata rather than inventing a different clip format

evals.prompt: Don't re-run Kokoro. Just rebuild the timing manifest from the WAVs already in evals/files/protected-clip/ using evals/files/segments.json and 0.25s padding. Write the manifest next to those WAVs in a temp copy if needed so the fixture stays intact.
evals.expected_output: Uses tts_manifest.py only (stdlib, no Kokoro/PyTorch). Measures existing WAV durations. Does not download models or run synthesize.py.
expectations: Does not import or run Kokoro, PyTorch, or SoundFile for this refresh
Does not run uv sync solely to refresh the manifest
Emits timeline fields from measured WAV headers

evals.prompt: Synthesize evals/files/segments.json into evals/files/protected-clip/. intro.wav is already there. Do not pass --overwrite.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to replace existing intro.wav. Reports the protected segment id. Does not delete or rewrite the fixture clip.
expectations: Does not replace or truncate the existing intro.wav
Reports the intro segment as protected / failed rather than silently skipping QA
Treats segment JSON as data, not executable input

evals.prompt: Narrate evals/files/mixed-voices.json with two speakers: host on af_bella and guest on bm_george. Don't force --lang-code; let each voice pick its pipeline.
evals.expected_output: Uses synthesize.py with per-segment voice ids from the JSON. Does not pass --lang-code. American and British voices are allowed in one job. Does not fall back to a cloud TTS vendor for the second speaker.
expectations: Reads mixed-voices.json and keeps both af_bella and bm_george
Does not pass --lang-code so language is derived from each voice
Does not invent a second TTS provider for the British speaker
Uses the bundled Kokoro catalog rather than guessing a new voice naming scheme
